correctness.rationale: The mixed power-sum expectation is reconstructed from beta moments of the first two size-biased Poisson–Dirichlet frequencies. Its analytic derivative at the Shannon endpoint gives the mixed logarithmic moment. Subtracting the independently verified means yields the stated rational covariance. The quadratic variance follows from the same mixed moment at equal exponents, and the trigamma asymptotic gives the limiting correlation. A deterministic high-precision checker independently evaluates the mixed moment by gamma differentiation and beta-log-moment formulas.

value.rationale: Shannon and Gini–Simpson indices are canonical companion summaries of random discrete diversity, and the literature commonly reports their marginal uncertainty separately. The exact covariance quantifies their redundancy under the central Poisson–Dirichlet prior family. The nonzero limiting correlation adds substantive structure: increasing concentration collapses the scale of both fluctuations but does not asymptotically decorrelate the two summaries.
